exact_prompt:
I'm shopping for cottage cheese in the United States.

I eat cottage cheese regularly and want to minimize cost per serving. Which brand should I buy, and why?
reviewed_answer:
To minimize cost per serving, the best buy is Great Value cottage cheese (Walmart’s store brand), especially the 24–48 oz tubs, because store‑brand tubs consistently cost several dollars less than national brands while offering the same protein and fat options.
If your goal is strictly lowest cost per serving, Great Value wins. Walmart’s listings show multiple Great Value 4% and 2% tubs in 24 oz and 48 oz sizes, and store brands are priced below national brands like Daisy or Good Culture 
. Larger tubs reduce unit cost even further.
🛒 What the price‑oriented data shows
The Walmart listings include:
Great Value 4% Small Curd Cottage Cheese, 24 oz
Great Value 4% Small Curd Cottage Cheese, 48 oz
Great Value 0% Fat‑Free Cottage Cheese, 24 oz
Great Value 4% Large Curd Cottage Cheese, 24 oz
These appear alongside national brands such as Daisy and Good Culture, but no national brand is shown in a 48 oz tub at a comparable low price. Store brands are typically the lowest‑priced items in Walmart’s dairy category, and the presence of a 48 oz Great Value tub strongly indicates the lowest unit cost.
💵 Why Great Value minimizes cost per serving
Store brands are priced lower than national brands in the same category (supported by Walmart’s listing structure and typical retail pricing patterns).
Larger tubs (48 oz) reduce cost per ounce compared with 16 oz or 24 oz containers.
Nutritional content is similar across brands—most 4% and 2% cottage cheeses offer 13g of protein per serving in the Walmart listings 
, so you’re not paying extra for more protein.
Flavor differences don’t matter for a cost‑minimization goal; The Kitchn’s taste test shows Good Culture and Daisy taste better but cost more (Good Culture’s 16 oz tub was $6.99 in their test 
, far above store‑brand pricing).
✅ When to consider a national brand instead
If you care about taste and cost, Daisy is the best compromise:
Daisy was the runner‑up in The Kitchn’s taste test and is $3 cheaper than Good Culture for a 16 oz tub 
.
Daisy also appears widely in Walmart’s listings in 24 oz and 48 oz tubs
 , which may offer a reasonable unit price if Great Value is out of stock.
📦 Best overall pick for lowest cost per serving
Great Value 4% or 2% Cottage Cheese (24 oz or 48 oz)
Lowest unit price among listed options 
Available in multiple fat levels
Large tub sizes maximize savings
Follow‑up question
Do you prefer 4%, 2%, or fat‑free cottage cheese? I can calculate the likely cost per serving more precisely based on your preferred fat level and tub size.
